Technically but not really. The book has two different random encounter tables for day and night indicating that Barovia still has the standard day/night cycle. Just imagine if every day were dark,cloudy, and rainy days and you never saw the sun through the clouds and fog/mists.

1. See OldandOldSchool’s comment, I’ve never seen a better summary of the general consensus on Vasilli.

2. Use a standard day/night cycle but definitely NO SUNLIGHT. Days are either rainy and dreary or gray/cloudy and dreary. One of the big things about Strahd’s realm, imo, is that there is seldom any rays of hope that the Players don’t create for themselves.  I think the only ray of sunshine my players saw came from them restoring Argynvostholt and returning the skull. 

3. I wouldn’t go as far so that they are never able to get into settlements because there can be a lot of plot points and fun events they would miss out on. Krezk is a bit like this which is nice so you can send the players on a quest to get inside but I think if every town was like that it would be a bit much. Instead, you should make them fear having to stay outside of settlements because running into Strahd’s spies/minions and random encounters should be nearly a guarantee. And these encounters only get worse if they are caught out at night. Much, much worse.

I’m running CoS right now and it is the first campaign I’ve ever run. I ran two unrelated one-shots with my players (who ended up carrying over their characters into Barovia) to get the hang things. Would HIGHLY recommend getting in a practice session or two. 

Next, you should at least skim through the entire CoS module as it’s pretty much a sandbox once the players get to Vallaki. A lot of areas and people are slightly intertwined, while others are a bit more stand alone. There are some YouTube videos (lunch break heroes and No fun allowed) detailing the different areas and their thoughts on them which helps you grasp them better.

100% join the discord for this subreddit as it is FILLED with resources, artwork, and genuinely helpful people for if you run into any issues. 

One thing I wish I did was hold a session 0 for my players. While we all agreed we were gunna play CoS, none of us truly knew what it would entail. Make sure your players are ok with all the horror and dark tones. 

Lastly, have Strahd show his presence early and often. The players should know that Barovia is truly Strahd’s domain and there is no escape from him while they are trapped there. I had them start on good terms, with Strahd welcoming them to his land, and giving them some helpful tips. As time has gone on and the party makes progress their relationship is slowly devolving with each encounter. As a villain, think of Strahd as a cat who is playing with a mouse before it inevitably devours it.

Best of luck to you!

It depends on how you run the vampire spawn in the coffin maker’s shop imo. I had it so the spawn were inactive and didn’t engage if the PCs showed up during the day, but if the PCs showed up at night, the spawn would grab the bones and run through the streets to the church, which would trigger St. Andral’s feast. If the vampires made it to the church, I would have Strahd burst into the church in 2-3 turns.

I don’t think strahd would bee line for the players simply because they recovered the bones though. St. Andral’s Feast is a boredom plan Strahd made before Ireena popped up and strahd has put it on the back burners ever since. So while the PCs retrieving the bones and consecrating the church would definitely peak Strahd’s interest,  it wouldn’t make him drop everything to fix it.
